We need be fair. The submission has many sections but some deficiencies. Need assess each criterion.

Actually SSO local time constraints; from 5°N, launch azimuth north-west/south-west? You can launch into retrograde orbit; RAAN precesses; there may be two launch opportunities per day for a given local time? But okay.
- Orbit: SSO at 600 km with inclination 97.79. Need check: For circular SSO, required inclination at 600 km is about 97.79°? Let's calculate: J2 precession = -3/2 J2 (Re/p)^2 n cos i = 360/365.25 deg/day = 0.9856 deg/day. At a=6971 km, n=sqrt(mu/a^3). Compute: mu=398600.4418; a=6971; a^3 = 3.387e11? 6971^3 = 3.387e11 (yes), n=sqrt(398600/3.387e11)=sqrt(1.177e-6)=0.0010848 rad/s = 93.65 rad/day? 0.0010848*86400=93.73 rad/day = 5370 deg/day. Factor -3/2 J2 (Re/a)^2 = -1.5*0.00108263*(6371/6971)^2 = -0.0016239*0.835? (6371/6971=0.914; squared=0.835) = -0.001356. times n=93.73 rad/day? Wait n in rad/day = 93.73 rad/day; product = -0.1271 rad/day = -7.28 deg/day. cos i = desired 0.9856 / 7.28 = 0.1354; i = 82.2° or 97.8°. Yes. So correct.
- It states RAAN 27.33° initial value indicates location of launch facility. But RAAN is not launch facility location; it's the right ascension of ascending node in inertial frame; not directly launch site. This is a technical error. Also RAAN will shift through all 360° every year; yes SSO.
- It says "Earth radius 6371 km plus proposed altitude 600 km = 6971 km"; okay.
- It gives argument of latitude 0° but no true anomaly/arg perigee. Fine.
- It says "constant supply of sunlight to satellite will be captured by solar panels" but SSO has eclipse periods; "descending side where satellite constantly in sunlight" is incorrect? In a SSO at 600 km, the satellite is in sunlight for a portion of each orbit depending on local time; not constantly on descending side. A dawn-dusk SSO can be in continuous sunlight, but this orbit's local time? RAAN initial 27.33 maybe not dawn-dusk. The ground track images show descending path? It labels "DN path for orbits 1-15" and says "where satellite is constantly in sunlight"; likely not true for all descending passes, especially at 600 km with 97.8° inclination and arbitrary RAAN; only if dawn-dusk. They don't specify local time of ascending node. This is a significant error. For SSO, lighting varies with season; at some seasons, eclipse. The "descending part" being sunlit is not guaranteed. The orbit's RAAN initial 27.33° may correspond to LTAN? Need compute: RAAN 27.33; Sun RA at Feb 3 ~315°? Local time of ascending node? Hmm. But no.
